mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 months signals monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present value of expected equity cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4% triggers a risk-off reaction, compressing discount rates and reducing expected equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals a labor market recovery, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in recovery periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -50,000 jobs triggers a risk-off reaction, compressing discount rates and reducing expected equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in weakness periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
